title: Value of an Asana OAuth access token in a token response or Bearer header
summary: A synthetic value of the access_token member of a pretty-printed token exchange response, and after Authorization: Bearer in a raw request and a quoted curl -H argument.
rationale: The carrier is documented: the Asana token exchange response is a JSON object whose access_token member holds the token, and the OAuth page shows the token passed in an Authorization: Bearer header. Asana says tokens are opaque and formats may change, and states no prefix, alphabet or length, so the value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only: the member name, the colon, the scheme word and the quotes are outside it. The expires_in number, the token_type word and the user object are not values of this credential.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the string value of the access_token member of a token exchange response, or the value after Authorization: Bearer, is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Asana documents the access_token response member and the Authorization: Bearer header (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The token to use in future requests against the API.
the application gets a token, which can be used in subsequent API calls through the addition of an Authorization header

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
